title: Test that task-sync export without a machine alias omits native activity
outcome: Test that task-sync export without a machine alias omits native activity
acceptance: A regression test creates native claim, release and completion history, exports without an origin-machine alias, and asserts every activity map is empty and the serialized task documents omit the activity key

completion.summary:
Added a regression test showing that task-sync export without a machine alias omits native activity.
- Item A is claimed and released; item B is claimed, then evidence, a checkpoint and completion.
- An aliased control export yields exactly A Released and B Finished.
- The alias-free export:
  - leaves every activity map empty;
  - counts no omissions and leaves the store unchanged;
  - writes no activity key in either task document;
  - matches the default export byte for byte.
- Files (test only): src/storage/work/task_sync/tests/activity.rs (+1 mod line) and src/storage/work/task_sync/tests/activity/without_alias.rs.
- Vacuity: a fallback-alias mutant and a no-skip_serializing_if mutant each fail the test.
- Reviews: two clean rounds (Codex 12260/12267, Claude 12261/12268).
